memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise." - Exodus 21:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This famous phrase is often misunderstood as a licence for revenge, but it is the opposite. In an age when a small offence could spark endless blood feuds — a life taken for a mere insult — God set a firm boundary: the punishment must fit the crime, and no more. "Eye for eye" was a leash on runaway vengeance, ensuring justice stayed measured and fair. It was mercy restraining rage.

Yet Jesus took us further still. He quoted these very words and then said, "But I tell you, do not resist an evil person" (Matt 5:38-39). He was not abolishing justice but calling His followers to a higher path — to absorb wrongs rather than always demand our due, to answer evil with grace. This is not weakness; it is the strength of a heart secure in God.

We see it perfectly in Jesus Himself. Wronged beyond measure, He did not retaliate but entrusted Himself to the Father who judges justly (1 Pet 2:23). At the cross, justice and mercy met — He bore the full penalty so that we could be forgiven. When someone wrongs you, you can release your right to revenge, because your Judge can be trusted, and your Saviour has already shown you the way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I holding on to a desire for revenge that God is asking me to release?
Where might God be calling me to answer wrong with grace instead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the just Judge, so I can let go of revenge. Give me the strength to answer wrong with grace, following the example of Jesus who forgave. Amen.
